document_chunks.content:
# Crunch Week starter pack

Everything you need to build against the Chilika Institute of Technology (CIT) dataset. Read the problem statement first; this file explains the data and the export format.

```
data/cit_public.json          the full dataset (one file, everything in it)
data/csv/*.csv                the same data as spreadsheets, for a quick look
validator.py                  the official validator (Python 3.8+, no installs)
examples/schedule.example.json   shape of the file you export (not a real solution)
examples/sample_disruption.json  practice disruption, same format as the live one
examples/sample_requests.md      plain-language requests to test your AI layer
```

Your app should read this file and change files in the format below, not hard-code anything from them. Judges will reset your app, generate the timetable themselves and apply change files of their own.

## Quick facts about the dataset

| Thing | Count |
| --- | --- |
| Rooms | 27 (classrooms, lecture halls, auditorium, seminar halls, open-air theatre, 7 labs) |
| Faculty | 40 |
| Student groups | 14 (Year 1 sections A to D, Year 2 and Year 3 for 5 branches) |
| Courses | 62 |
| Sessions to schedule | 189 (243 teaching hours a week) |
| Spectra week booking requests | 25 (one of them is cancelled) |
| Midsem exams | 41 |

A timetable with zero hard violations exists for this dataset. We checked.

## Time model

- Days: `MON` to `FRI`.
- Periods `1` to `9` are teaching periods, one hour each: P1 08:00, P2 09:00 ... P5 12:00, lunch 13:00 to 14:00, P6 14:00 ... P9 17:00.
- Periods `10` to `13` (18:00 to 22:00) are for events only.
- A session with `duration` d placed at `start_period` p occupies p, p+1, ... p+d-1. It may not span P5 and P6 (lunch).
- Labs (`kind: "lab"`, 3 hours) start only at P2 or P6.
## The dataset, field by field

### rooms
`id`, `name`, `building`, `type`, `capacity`, `features`, `accessible`, `allowed_uses`.

Room `type` is one of `classroom`, `lecture_hall`, `auditorium`, `seminar_hall`, `outdoor`, `lab_cs`, `lab_elec`, `lab_phy`, `workshop`, `lab_civil`. `allowed_uses` says whether a room can take lectures, tutorials, labs, exams or events. Seminar halls and the open-air theatre never take regular classes.

### room_unavailability
`room_id`, `day`, `periods`, `reason`. The room can't be used at those times.

### faculty
`id`, `name`, `department`, `max_hours_per_day` (hard limit), `needs_accessible`, `unavailable` (list of `day` + `periods`, hard), `preferences` (soft).

A preference looks like `{"type": "avoid", "days": [...], "periods": [...], "note": "..."}`. Each hour a faculty member teaches inside an avoided day and period costs 2 points (S1).

### student_groups
`id`, `name`, `year`, `department`, `size`, `needs_accessible`.

### courses
Reference information: `lecture_hours`, `tutorial_hours`, `lab_blocks` per week. You don't schedule courses; you schedule sessions.

### sessions — the thing you schedule
```json
{
  "id": "MA101-AB-L1",
  "course_id": "MA101",
  "kind": "lecture",               // lecture | tutorial | lab
  "groups": ["Y1-A", "Y1-B"],      // every group that must attend
  "faculty_id": "F19",
  "size": 180,                     // students attending
  "duration": 1,                   // periods
  "room_types": ["classroom", "lecture_hall", "auditorium"],
  "needs_accessible": false,
  "basket_slot": null,             // e.g. "OEB-1" for open electives
  "fixed_slot": null               // e.g. {"day": "THU", "start_period": 6} = must go exactly there
}
```
Each session needs exactly one `day`, `start_period` and `room_id`. Faculty are already assigned.

**Elective baskets.** Year 3 students each take one of three open electives (OE301, OE302, OE303). The three courses run in parallel: every session with the same `basket_slot` must be at the same day and period, in different rooms. Their `groups` lists all Year 3 groups because each group has students in all three. Sessions in the same basket slot don't clash with each other for groups; they do clash with everything else those groups have.
## 4. Special Subsystems

### booking_requests — Spectra week (Week 7)
```json
{
  "id": "BR-07",
  "submitted_at": "2027-01-26T09:45:00+05:30",
  "requester": "Dramatics Society",
  "role": "club",                         // admin | department_coordinator | faculty | club
  "requested_category": "club_event",
  "title": "Stage play: Andha Yug",
  "attendance": 130,
  "duration_periods": 3,
  "windows": [{"day": "THU", "from_period": 10, "to_period": 12}],
  "room_types": ["seminar_hall", "auditorium"],
  "needs": ["stage", "pa_system"],        // "accessible" means the room must be accessible
  "requested_room": "SH-1",               // a wish, may be null, may not even exist
  "mandatory_for_groups": [],             // these groups must be free
  "series_id": null,
  "raw_text": "Dramatics needs SH-1 Thursday 6 to 9 pm ..."
}
```
A booking must fit fully inside one window to be approved. `raw_text` is the original message, so it doubles as test input for your plain-language parser.

**Category is capped by role.** `role_category_cap` in the dataset says the highest category each role may claim. A club asking for `institute_event` is still a `club_event`. Priority order is in `priority_order`; ties go to the earlier `submitted_at`.

**cancellations** lists requests withdrawn after submission. Never approve those.

### exams
`id`, `course_ids`, `groups`, `size`, `duration_hours`. Exam week is `MON` to `SAT` with sessions `AM` (09:30 to 11:30) and `PM` (14:00 to 16:00), in `calendar.exam_week`. Rooms seat half their capacity during exams; an exam may use several rooms.

## Running the validator

```
python validator.py --data data/cit_public.json --schedule schedule.json
python validator.py --data data/cit_public.json --schedule schedule.json --json report.json
```

Checking a change: apply `examples/sample_disruption.json` in your app, export the repaired timetable, then

```
python validator.py --data data/cit_public.json --schedule schedule_after.json \
                    --disruption examples/sample_disruption.json --baseline schedule.json
```

It prints hard violations by rule, the soft penalty (S1 to S6), the booking score, priority inversions (you rejected someone who should have won a room), and how many sessions moved.

### Disruption file format
```json
{"changes": [
  {"type": "faculty_unavailable", "faculty_id": "F07", "days": ["MON"], "periods": [1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9], "reason": "..."},
  {"type": "room_unavailable", "room_id": "CR-102", "days": ["MON","TUE"], "periods": [1,2,3], "reason": "..."},
  {"type": "add_faculty", "faculty": { ...same shape as a faculty entry... }},
  {"type": "add_session", "session": { ...same shape as a session, may have fixed_slot... }},
  {"type": "remove_session", "session_id": "HS201-H2-L2"}
]}
```
Changes are permanent: they hold for every week after they're applied.

If you think the validator is wrong, tell the organisers during the hackathon.

## What goes in your exports/ folder

Commit both of these to your repo before the deadline:

- `exports/schedule.json`: your app's output for `cit_public.json` (timetable, exams and Spectra week bookings).
- `exports/schedule_after.json`: the timetable after applying `examples/sample_disruption.json` in your app, starting from that `schedule.json`.

Both must be produced by the app. Files made or edited by hand lead to disqualification.

document_chunks.section_title: CampusOS Scheduling Intelligence & AI System Specifications
document_chunks.content: # CampusOS Scheduling Intelligence & AI System Specifications

## Chilika Institute of Technology (CIT) — CrunchWeek

---

## 1. Architectural Philosophy & Principle

> **Core architectural principle: AI understands and communicates. Deterministic engines validate and decide.**

In CampusOS:
- **LLM / AI Layer** handles natural-language parsing (English and Hinglish), intent extraction, user interaction, explanation generation, and RAG retrieval over institutional policies.
- **Deterministic Engines (Google OR-Tools CP-SAT)** model the mathematical constraint satisfaction and optimization problem (CSP/COP), finding globally optimal or strictly feasible assignments.
- **Official Validator (`validator.py`)** is the sole and ultimate ground truth for schedule validity and penalty metrics. No solution is considered valid until `validator.py` evaluates it with zero hard violations.

---
## 2. Temporal & Spatial Problem Model

### 2.1 Calendar & Period Discretization
Regular academic schedule operates across 5 days:
$$\text{Days} = \{\text{MON}, \text{TUE}, \text{WED}, \text{THU}, \text{FRI}\}$$

Discretized daily periods $p \in \{1, 2, \dots, 13\}$:
- **Teaching Periods (Regular Classes):** $P1$ through $P9$ ($p \in [1, 9]$)
  - $P1$: 08:00 – 09:00
  - $P2$: 09:00 – 10:00
  - $P3$: 10:00 – 11:00
  - $P4$: 11:00 – 12:00
  - $P5$: 12:00 – 13:00
  - **Lunch Interval:** 13:00 – 14:00 (strictly after $P5$, before $P6$)
  - $P6$: 14:00 – 15:00
  - $P7$: 15:00 – 16:00
  - $P8$: 16:00 – 17:00
  - $P9$: 17:00 – 18:00
- **Evening Event Periods:** $P10$ through $P13$ ($p \in [10, 13]$, 18:00 – 22:00) reserved exclusively for events and bookings.

### 2.2 Dataset Entities
- **Rooms ($R = 27$):** Classified by `type` (`classroom`, `lecture_hall`, `auditorium`, `seminar_hall`, `outdoor`, `lab_cs`, `lab_elec`, `lab_phy`, `workshop`, `lab_civil`), `capacity`, `features` (e.g., `projector`, `stage`, `pa_system`, `wifi`, `computers`), `accessible` (boolean flag), and `allowed_uses` (subset of `{"lecture", "tutorial", "lab", "exam", "event"}`).
- **Faculty ($F = 40$):** Attributes include `max_hours_per_day` (default 4), `needs_accessible`, hard `unavailable` blocks, and soft `preferences` (penalty avoidance blocks).
- **Student Groups ($G = 14$):** Cohorts including Year 1 (`Y1-A` through `Y1-D`), Year 2 and Year 3 departmental branches (`CSE-2`, `CSE-3`, `ECE-2`, `ECE-3`, `ME-2`, `ME-3`, `CE-2`, `CE-3`, `EE-2`, `EE-3`).
- **Sessions ($S = 189$):** 153 lectures, 27 labs (3-hour blocks), 9 tutorials (1-hour blocks). Each session $s \in S$ requires assigning $(day, start\_period, room\_id)$.
- **Exams ($E = 41$):** Midsem exams occurring in dedicated exam week (MON–SAT, AM/PM sessions).
- **Spectra Week Bookings ($B = 25$):** Event booking requests during Week 7 with role priority caps.

---
## 3. Official Validator Constraint Catalog

### 3.1 Hard Constraints (Zero Violations Permitted)

| Code | Rule Description | Mathematical / Logic Formulation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **H1** | **Session Existence & Validity** | Every session $s \in S$ must be scheduled exactly once. Day $\in \{\text{MON}\dots\text{FRI}\}$, room $r \in R$, session id must exist in dataset and appear at most once. |
| **H2** | **Faculty Clash Prevention** | A faculty member $f$ cannot teach multiple sessions concurrently: $\sum_{s \in S(f)} \mathbb{I}(p \in \text{periods}(s)) \le 1, \quad \forall (f, day, p)$. |
| **H3** | **Student Group Clash Prevention** | A student group $g$ cannot attend overlapping sessions, **except** sessions sharing the identical `basket_slot`. Distinct session keys occupying $(g, day, p)$ must be $\le 1$. |
| **H4** | **Room Clash Prevention** | A room $r$ can host at most one teaching session at any $(day, p)$: $\sum_{s \in S(r)} \mathbb{I}(p \in \text{periods}(s)) \le 1$. |
| **H5** | **Room Capacity** | Room capacity must accommodate session size: $\text{capacity}(r) \ge \text{size}(s)$. |
| **H6** | **Room Type Compatibility** | Assigned room type must belong to session's allowed types: $\text{type}(r) \in \text{room\_types}(s)$. |
| **H7** | **Faculty Unavailability** | No session can occupy a $(day, p)$ where assigned faculty $f(s)$ is marked unavailable in `faculty.unavailable`. |
| **H8** | **Room Unavailability** | No session can occupy $(day, p)$ where assigned room $r$ is marked unavailable in `room_unavailability`. |
| **H9** | **Session Timing & Boundary** | $start \ge 1$ and $start + \text{duration}(s) - 1 \le 9$. A session cannot span across lunch ($P5$ and $P6$ simultaneously). Labs ($\text{duration} = 3$) must start strictly at $P2$ or $P6$. |
| **H10** | **Accessibility Mandate** | If session has $\text{needs\_accessible} = \text{true}$, assigned room must have $\text{accessible} = \text{true}$. |
| **H11** | **Elective Basket Synchronization** | All sessions belonging to the same `basket_slot` (e.g. `OEB-1`, `OEB-2`, `OEB-3`) must be scheduled at the exact same $(day, start\_period)$. |
| **H12** | **Faculty Daily Teaching Limits** | Daily teaching hours for faculty $f$ on any day cannot exceed `max_hours_per_day` (typically 4 hours). |
| **H14** | **Fixed Slot Compliance** | If session specifies `fixed_slot = {"day": d, "start_period": p}`, it must be assigned exactly to $(d, p)$. |

### 3.2 Soft Constraints & Penalty Formulation

The timetable objective minimizes total soft penalty:
$$\min \sum_{k=1}^6 \text{Pen}(S_k)$$

| Code | Soft Rule | Penalty Formula in Validator | CP-SAT Modeling Strategy |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **S1** | **Faculty Preferences** | $+2$ points per teaching hour occurring inside an avoided $(day, p)$ from `faculty.preferences`. | Add linear penalty terms: $2 \times \text{duration} \times \mathbb{I}(d, p \text{ in pref})$. |
| **S2** | **Student Group Gaps** | $+1$ point per idle period between a group's first and last period on any day: $\sum_{p=\min(P_g)}^{\max(P_g)} \mathbb{I}(p \notin P_g)$. | Model daily start period $\min_g$, end period $\max_g$, and span minus total hours. |
| **S3** | **Student Daily Overload** | $+3$ points per hour taught beyond 6 hours in a single day for any student group: $3 \times \max(0, \text{hours}(g, day) - 6)$. | Constrain or heavily penalize daily group load $> 6$. |
| **S4** | **Same-Course Multiple Lectures** | $+3$ points for each lecture of the same course beyond the 1st on the same day for a student group: $3 \times \max(0, \text{count} - 1)$. | Penalty for duplicate course lectures on the same day. |
| **S5** | **Room Under-utilization** | $+1$ point per session if $\text{size}(s) / \text{capacity}(r) < 0.4$. | Penalize assignments of small classes to huge lecture halls / auditoriums when classrooms fit. |
| **S6** | **Late Evening Teaching** | $+1$ point per session occupying Period 9 ($P9$, 17:00–18:00). | Add binary indicator penalty variable for sessions spanning $P9$. |

---

### 4.1 Elective Baskets (Open Electives)
- Open Electives (e.g. `OE301`, `OE302`, `OE303` in `OEB-1`, `OEB-2`, `OEB-3`) run simultaneously.
- Every Year 3 student group is listed on all sessions in the basket because students split across electives.
- **Key distinction:** `validator.py` uses `key = s.get("basket_slot") or sid`. Multiple basket sessions at the same $(day, p)$ share the same key and therefore **do not clash with each other** for groups, but they **strictly clash** with any non-basket class or differing basket for Year 3.
- All sessions in basket $b$ must have identical $(day, start)$.

### 4.2 Spectra Week Bookings (Fest Week)
- Decisions must be one of: `approved`, `rejected`, or `alternative_offered`.
- Rejections and alternatives require a non-empty human-readable `reason`.
- Role-based category capping applies:
  - `admin` $\to$ `institute_event`
  - `faculty` $\to$ `guest_lecture`
  - `department_coordinator` $\to$ `department_event`
  - `club` $\to$ `club_event`
- Priority order: `["exam", "regular_session", "institute_event", "guest_lecture", "department_event", "club_event"]`.
- Priority tie-breaker: earlier `submitted_at` timestamp.
- **Priority Inversions:** The validator penalizes rejecting a higher-priority request if its requirements could have been met in a slot allocated to a lower-priority booking.
- **Session Overrides:** Only approved `institute_event` may displace a regular teaching session. Displaced sessions must be relocated to another valid, clash-free slot.

### 4.3 Exam Scheduling
- Calendar: Monday to Saturday, sessions `AM` (09:30–11:30) and `PM` (14:00–16:00).
- Multiple rooms may be assigned to an exam.
- **Half-Capacity Rule:** Room seats during exams $= \lfloor \text{capacity}(r) / 2 \rfloor$.
- Exam rooms must have `"exam"` in `allowed_uses`.
- Hard constraints: No room double-booked in same $(day, session)$, no group double-booked in same $(day, session)$, total seats $\ge \text{size}(e)$.
- Exam soft penalty: $+5$ points for each exam beyond the 1st on the same day for any group.

### 4.4 Disruption Handling & Stability
- Disruption types: `faculty_unavailable`, `room_unavailable`, `add_faculty`, `add_session`, `remove_session`.
- Evaluation metrics:
  - `sessions_moved`: count of sessions where $(day, start, room)$ changed from baseline.
  - `time_changed`: session changed day or start period.
  - `room_only_changed`: session kept day and start period, only room relocated.
- Objective: Satisfy all post-disruption hard constraints while minimizing `sessions_moved`.

---

## 5. Backend Integration Interface Contract

The intelligence module exposes clean, stateless, FastAPI-compatible interfaces:

```python

# Timetable Generation & Validation
generate_timetable(
    data: dict, options: TimetableOptions | None = None
) -> TimetableResult
validate_timetable(
    schedule: dict, data: dict, baseline: dict | None = None
) -> ValidationReport

# Rescheduling Engine
reschedule(
    baseline: dict, disruption: dict, data: dict, options: RescheduleOptions
) -> RescheduleResult

# Exam Engine
generate_exam_schedule(
    data: dict, options: ExamOptions | None = None
) -> ExamResult

# Fest Week Booking Engine
evaluate_bookings(
    data: dict, timetable: dict, options: BookingOptions | None = None
) -> FestWeekResult

# Natural Language Assistant & RAG
process_assistant_message(
    message: str,
    user_context: UserContext,
    conversation_history: list[ChatMessage],
) -> AssistantResponse
```

# Sample plain-language requests (public)

Practice inputs for your AI layer. Every `raw_text` field in the dataset's booking requests is also a test input.
The judges use a different, harder set when they test your app.

For each one, your app should produce an editable structured booking, or ask a follow-up question when something essential is missing.

1. Need a room for 45 people on Tuesday 6 to 8 pm, projector please.
2. Book the auditorium for the CSE department farewell, Friday evening, around 400 people, need stage and mic.
3. Can I get a lab with computers for a 3-hour coding contest on Thursday afternoon? About 60 participants.
4. Our club meets every Monday and Wednesday 7 to 8 pm, 30 people, any small room is fine.
5. Mechanical third years need a 2 hour session with an industry speaker on Wednesday, it's compulsory for them.
6. seminar hall kal shaam 6 baje, 2 ghante, 100 log, mic chahiye
7. I want SH-2 on Friday at 10 am for a wheelchair-accessible poster session, 60 people.
8. Need somewhere for the quiz finals after lunch on Thursday, maybe 150 people.

document_chunks.section_title: Expected structure for three of them
document_chunks.content:
### Expected structure for three of them

Request 1:
```json
{"attendance": 45, "duration_periods": 2,
 "windows": [{"day": "TUE", "from_period": 10, "to_period": 11}],
 "needs": ["projector"], "room_types": ["classroom", "lecture_hall", "seminar_hall"],
 "mandatory_for_groups": [], "follow_up": null}
```

Request 6 ("seminar hall tomorrow 6 pm, 2 hours, 100 people, need a mic"):
```json
{"attendance": 100, "duration_periods": 2,
 "windows": [{"day": "<tomorrow's weekday>", "from_period": 10, "to_period": 11}],
 "needs": ["pa_system"], "room_types": ["seminar_hall"], "follow_up": null}
```
"Kal" can mean yesterday or tomorrow in Hindi. In a booking request it means tomorrow, and the app should resolve it to a weekday.

Request 7: SH-2 is not wheelchair accessible. A good system notices the conflict between the named room and the stated need, and offers SH-1 instead of silently booking SH-2.

Request 8 is vague about time and size. "After lunch" could be P6 onward. A good system either asks, or proposes a window and makes the assumption visible in the editable form.
